terms.meaning: A drawing area in a web page that code paints onto.
Temporary stand-in content shown until the real content is ready.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Placeholder artwork file header
sections.what: A comment stating that the file draws labelled placeholder artwork for media slots that have no real asset.
sections.why: Explains the purpose of the file to anyone reading it.

sections.name: PlaceholderSpec
sections.title: Information needed for one placeholder
sections.what: The data a placeholder needs: a title, a code, a label and a seed number.
sections.why: Keeps all placeholder data in one shape.
sections.watch_out: The seed decides the picture, so changing it changes that slot's artwork.

sections.name: rng
sections.title: Repeatable random numbers for artwork
sections.what: Creates repeatable random numbers from a seed. This is a copy of the same kind of helper used in the industry sheet file.
sections.why: Gives each placeholder the same look every time it is drawn.
sections.watch_out: Fixes to one copy do not reach the other copy.

sections.name: drawPlaceholder (part 1)
sections.title: Background, light and panels
sections.what: Sizes the canvas, then paints a dark gradient, a soft light spot, a faint grid and a set of random interface-style panels.
sections.why: Makes the placeholder resemble a dark interface mock-up.
sections.watch_out: If the canvas has no 2D drawing context, nothing is drawn and no error is shown.

sections.name: drawPlaceholder: for
sections.title: Rings, title and labels
sections.what: Draws concentric rings and a crosshair, then the large title, a code label, a note telling the reader to replace the placeholder in the assets file, and the coordinates.
sections.why: Marks the image clearly as a placeholder.
sections.watch_out: The replace note is fixed text, so it becomes wrong if the assets file moves or is renamed.

summary: Draws a dark, labelled placeholder picture for media slots that have no real asset yet.
purpose: Keeps the layout whole while real images are missing, and makes clear that they are placeholders.
why: The header describes it as clearly labelled placeholder artwork for empty media slots.
how: Given a canvas and a spec, sets the size, then paints a gradient, a soft light spot, a faint grid, random interface-style panels, concentric rings, a large title, labels, a replace-me note and coordinates.
inputs: A canvas element, a PlaceholderSpec object, a width and a height.
outputs: Paints onto the canvas. Returns nothing.
risks: Does nothing when the canvas has no 2D drawing context. The placeholder note names a file path that must be updated if that file moves.
debug: If no picture appears, check that a canvas was passed and that a spec was supplied. If the text looks wrong, check whether the named font loaded.
